title: Enterprise Onboarding & Support Playbook - Onboarding, Escalation, Integration, Known Issues, QBRs
author: Evelyn Chen
body:
Overview

This playbook provides a single, pragmatic reference for enterprise onboarding, integration validation, escalation procedures, common known issues and workarounds, and Quarterly Business Review (QBR) materials for Redwood Inference customers. It is authoritative for Customer Success (CS) engagements and cross-functional support during the first 90 days of an enterprise relationship and ongoing health checks.

Scope
- Applies to all new Dedicated and Private deployment customers and self-serve Hosted customers moving to enterprise support.
- Covers: onboarding phases, integration checkpoints, production readiness gates, escalation matrix and runbooks, known issues + workarounds, and QBR reporting templates.

Goals
- Reduce time-to-value and time-to-first-successful-production-call to <= 30 days for standard integrations.
- Ensure 99.95% availability for billed endpoints per contract and measurable health signals for QBR discussions.
- Provide clear escalation paths to resolve Sev1 incidents within 4 hours (initial response) and drive root-cause to full remediation within the SLA window.

Ownership and Contacts
- Playbook owner: Customer Success (owner_team). Primary owner: Evelyn Chen (author).
- Escalation owners: Eng SRE (oncall rotation), Eng Platform (integrations), Eng Serving Runtime (model-serving regressions).
- Primary channels: Slack #cs-enterprise, #ops-oncall; Email: support@redwood.com; PagerDuty: Redwood-SRE-prod.

Onboarding Phases & Checklist (90-day template)
1) Sales-to-CS Handoff (Day 0)
   - Deliverables: contract, SSO info, allowed IP ranges, compliance requirements, data residency spec.
   - Actions: create customer workspace in Console, enable billing account, provision initial API keys (scoped).
2) Technical Kickoff (Day 1-7)
   - Attendees: CS, Solutions Eng, Customer Engineer, Security POC.
   - Agenda: architecture review, network/firewall requirements, model selection, expected QPS/latency, failure modes.
   - Outcomes: Integration plan, milestone dates.
3) Integration & Validation (Day 7-30)
   - API smoke tests: token generation, single-request generation, embeddings, streaming.
   - Integration checklist (must-pass before staging):
     - Auth: API key or OAuth SSO validated.
     - Networking: egress/ingress allowed to Redwood endpoints in chosen region.
     - Observability: Redwood Console access, set up dashboards, link to customer metrics.
     - Load tests: baseline QPS and seq-len distribution recorded.
4) Staging Rollout (Day 30-60)
   - Canary traffic plan, circuit-breaker thresholds, autoscaling config for Dedicated.
   - Validation: latency p95 under SLA target, error rate < 0.1% in staging.
5) Production Cutover (Day 60-90)
   - Final checklist: data retention/KMS keys, audit logging enabled, runbook distributed to customer support, QBR schedule.

Integration Guide - Key Endpoints & Configuration (summary)
- Service names: Redwood API (hosted inference), Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity), Redwood Console (observability).
- Common endpoints: POST /v1/generate, POST /v1/chat, POST /v1/embeddings, GET /v1/health.

Required headers and example:
- Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>
- Content-Type: application/json

Example curl (text generation):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-2-medium", "input":"Summarize: ...", "max_tokens":256}'

Configuration table (minimum integration config)
| Setting | Recommended value | Notes |
|--------|-------------------|-------|
| Region | us-west-2 | Match customer region for residency |
| Model | redwood-2-medium / curated open model | Start with medium for latency-sensitive apps |
| Auth | API Key + IP allowlist | Use scoped keys for third-party integrations |
| Logging | Audit logs enabled | 90-day retention for enterprise by default |

SLOs & Health thresholds (Customer-facing targets)
- Availability: 99.95% (rolling 30d) for provisioned endpoints.
- Latency: p50 < 40ms, p95 < 150ms for text generation on Dedicated baseline configs.
- Error rate: < 0.1% 4xx/5xx for steady-state traffic.
- Embeddings: p95 < 300ms.

Escalation Playbook (Severity definitions and steps)
- Sev1 (Critical): Complete outage for customer production traffic or data loss risk.
  1. Initial action: CS oncall & SRE notify, open incident in Incident Response tool; 15-minute response target.
  2. Triage: Run health checks (GET /v1/health), check cluster autoscale, check queue backpressure metrics.
  3. Mitigation: Rollback recent canary, route to fallback model/region, increase capacity from Dedicated burst pool.
  4. Communication: Hourly status updates to customer and internal exec channel until resolved.
  5. Postmortem: Document within 72 hours, include timeline, root cause, corrective action owners.
- Sev2 (High): Partial degradation (elevated latency or errors impacting some requests).
  1. Initial action: SRE/Platform respond within 30 minutes, CS provides customer impact summary.
  2. Triage: Check latency distribution, batching backlog, KV cache hit rates.
  3. Mitigation: Tune batching window, enable prefix caching, temporarily scale workers.
  4. Communication: Update customer + internal channel every 2 hours.
- Sev3 (Medium): Functional issue with workaround available.
  1. Owner: CS or Solutions Eng triages and applies workaround; target next-business-day fix.

Escalation matrix (who to page)
- CS Lead -> Solutions Eng -> Eng Platform -> Eng SRE -> Eng Serving Runtime -> CTO (if > 8 hours unresolved for Sev1).

Runbook: Immediate troubleshooting checklist (to run in order)
1. Verify customer API key validity and auth logs in Console.
2. Run GET /v1/health and check region-specific health.
3. Check Redwood Console dashboards: request rate, error rate, queue depth, GPU utilization.
4. Inspect recent deploys/rollouts (Console -> Rollouts) for failed canaries.
5. For Dedicated: check node health in infra console and node-level metrics.
6. If model regression suspected: execute quick compare (baseline prompt set vs. current) and rollback model version.

Known Issues & Workarounds (select common items)
| Issue | Symptom | Workaround / Temporary Mitigation | Owner |
|-------|---------|------------------------------------|-------|
| Memory pressure on long-sequence requests | OOMs on worker, p95 spikes | Enforce max_sequence_length, enable KV streaming, split requests | Eng Serving Runtime |
| Elevated 5xx during autoscaling | Thundering scaling events cause queue overflow | Implement gradual scaling config, enable burst capacity | Eng Platform |
| Higher latency for small-batch embeddings | p95 high due to batching thresholds | Lower batching window for embeddings, enable dedicated embedding nodes | Eng Infra |
| Tokenization mismatches for non-UTF8 inputs | Unexpected model tokens / truncation | Normalize input to UTF-8, pre-tokenize in client | Solutions Eng |

Permanent fixes should be tracked in Jira with component tagging (component: serving-runtime / infra / platform). For customer-facing workarounds, create a support ticket and notify CS manager.

Health Checks & QBR Materials
- Dashboards to configure in Redwood Console for QBR:
  - Request volume and top endpoints (30d, 90d)
  - Latency percentiles (p50, p95, p99) per model/version
  - Error rates and top error codes (4xx/5xx)
  - Cost per request / token (token-level cost)
  - Model quality signals: prompt-set eval regressions, hallucination rate (customer-provided evals)

- Suggested QBR cadence and agenda (Quarterly)
  1. Opening summary: adoption metrics and business outcomes (10m)
  2. Reliability review: availability, incidents, mitigations (15m)
  3. Performance & cost: latency trends, cost per request, optimization opportunities (15m)
  4. Quality & model roadmap: eval results, recommended model/quantization changes (15m)
  5. Action items and next steps: owners and deadlines (10m)

Templates and Attachments (links to create)
- Integration validation checklist (CSV) - use for staging signoff.
- Escalation contact matrix (spreadsheet).
- QBR slide deck template (pptx) with pre-built charts (use Redwood Console exports).
- Postmortem template (markdown).

On-call Handoff & After-action
- After any Sev1/Sev2 incident, the owning team must complete the postmortem template within 72 hours and assign remediation owners with ETA.
- CS must run a customer-facing RCA call within 7 business days for Sev1 incidents.

FAQs (short)
- Q: What is the fastest way to reduce tail latency?
  A: Enable KV caching, reduce batching window for latency-sensitive routes, pin a smaller model for that route.
- Q: How do we validate model quality regressions?
  A: Run the customer prompt-set through the eval harness in applied-ml-and-evals; compare metrics against baseline and open a regression-triage ticket if delta exceeds threshold.
